    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(recentWindow)
    | where DeviceVendor == "Zscaler" and DeviceProduct has "ZPA"
    | where isnotempty(SourceUserName)
    | extend RecentCountry = tostring(geo_info_from_ip_address(SourceIP).country)
    | summarize
        RecentCountries = make_set(RecentCountry, 5),
        RecentApps      = make_set(DestinationHostName, 10),
        RecentIPs       = make_set(SourceIP, 5),
        RecentConnCount = count(),
        ZPA_FirstSeen   = min(TimeGenerated)
      by UserName = tolower(SourceUserName);
let ZIA_Suspicious =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(recentWindow)
    | where DeviceVendor == "Zscaler"
    | where isnotempty(SourceUserName)
    | where DeviceCustomString2 has_any (
        "REMOTE_ACCESS_TOOLS", "REMOTE_ADMINISTRATION", "WEB_BASED_ADMIN",
        "ACCOUNT_CREATION", "TUNNEL_SOCKS_PROXY", "ANONYMOUS_PROXY",
        "ONLINE_STORAGE", "FILE_SHARE", "TOR", "VPN_SERVICES",
        "NEWLY_REGISTERED_DOMAINS", "PHISHING")
    | summarize
        ZIA_Categories   = make_set(DeviceCustomString2, 10),
        ZIA_Destinations = make_set(DestinationHostName, 10),
        ZIA_RequestCount = count(),
        ZIA_FirstSeen    = min(TimeGenerated)
      by UserName = tolower(SourceUserName);
let IdP_Changes =
    OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(recentWindow)
    | where isnotempty(UserId)
    | where Operation in (
        "New-InboxRule",
        "Set-Mailbox",
        "Add-MailboxPermission",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",
        "Consent to application",
        "Add service principal credentials",
        "Update user",
        "Disable Strong Authentication",
        "Update StsRefreshTokenValidFrom",
        "Add member to role")
    | summarize
        IdP_EventCount = count(),
        IdP_Operations = make_set(Operation, 10),
        IdP_FirstSeen  = min(TimeGenerated)
      by UserName = tolower(UserId);
ZPA_Recent
| join kind=inner ZPA_Baseline on UserName
| extend NewCountries = set_difference(RecentCountries, BaselineCountries)
| join kind=leftouter ZIA_Suspicious on UserName
| join kind=leftouter IdP_Changes on UserName
| extend
    ZIA_RequestCount = coalesce(ZIA_RequestCount, 0),
    IdP_EventCount   = coalesce(IdP_EventCount, 0)
| extend ImpostorScore =
    iff(array_length(NewCountries) > 0, 40, 0)
  + (ZIA_RequestCount * 5)
  + (IdP_EventCount * 30)
| where ImpostorScore >= 40
    or (IdP_EventCount >= 1 and ZIA_RequestCount >= 1)
    or array_length(NewCountries) > 0
| project
    UserName,
    NewCountries, RecentCountries, BaselineCountries,
    RecentApps, RecentIPs, RecentConnCount,
    ZIA_Categories, ZIA_Destinations, ZIA_RequestCount,
    IdP_Operations, IdP_EventCount,
    ImpostorScore,
    ZPA_FirstSeen
| order by ImpostorScore desc

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: User {{UserName}} shows cross-layer anomalies: new countries {{NewCountries}}, {{ZIA_RequestCount}} ZIA suspicious requests, {{IdP_EventCount}} identity/security changes. ImpostorScore: {{ImpostorScore}}.

properties.displayName: Zscaler ZIA - APT Control Evasion: Agent Tampering and Visibility Degradation
properties.description: Detects an attacker (or insider) attempting to degrade SOC visibility by breaking Zscaler or EDR telemetry. This "maximum paranoia mode" rule correlates two distinct evidence streams: 1. VISIBILITY LOSS: Hosts that had consistent ZIA traffic in the prior 7-day baseline (â‰¥10 requests/day) but produced zero ZIA telemetry in the most recent 4-hour window, without a known global outage explanation. 2. AGENT TAMPERING: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint (DeviceEvents) service-stop / service-delete / driver-unload events targeting Zscaler Client Connector or EDR agent processes (ZscalerService, ZSATunnel, ZSAUpdater, MsSense, SenseSvc). SecurityEvent Windows Service Control Manager events (EventID 7034-7045) for the same service names are also correlated. Both streams are scored jointly. A disappearing host alone warrants investigation; a disappearing host with corroborating agent-tamper events is a critical indicator of deliberate control evasion aligned with MITRE T1562 (Impair Defenses) and T1070 (Indicator Removal). Outcome: A ranked list of source IPs / hosts showing evidence of being "detached" from the Zero Trust / Zscaler architecture for manual investigation and potential endpoint isolation. MITRE ATT&CK: TA0005 (Defense Evasion), T1562 (Impair Defenses), T1562.001 (Disable or Modify Tools), T1070 (Indicator Removal).
properties.query:
let baselineWindow            = 7d;
let recentWindow              = 4h;
let minBaselineRequestsPerDay = 10;
let ZIA_BaselineHosts =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(baselineWindow) .. ago(recentWindow))
    | where DeviceVendor == "Zscaler"
    | where isnotempty(SourceIP) and isnotempty(SourceUserName)
    | summarize
        BaselineRequestsPerDay = round(toreal(count()) / (baselineWindow / 1d), 1),
        BaselineUsers          = make_set(SourceUserName, 5)
      by SourceIP
    | where BaselineRequestsPerDay >= minBaselineRequestsPerDay;
let ZIA_RecentActive =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(recentWindow)
    | where DeviceVendor == "Zscaler"
    | where isnotempty(SourceIP)
    | distinct SourceIP;
let SilentHosts =
    ZIA_BaselineHosts
    | join kind=leftanti ZIA_RecentActive on SourceIP;
let AgentTampering =
    DeviceEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(recentWindow)
    | where ActionType in (
        "ServiceUninstalled", "ServiceStopped", "DriverUnloaded",
        "TamperingAttempt", "AntivirusScanFailed")
      or (ActionType == "ProcessCreated"
          and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (
              "ZscalerApp", "ZSATunnel", "ZSAUpdater", "ZscalerService",
              "sc stop", "sc delete", "net stop", "taskkill"))
    | summarize
        TamperEvents    = count(),
        TamperActions   = make_set(ActionType, 10),
        TamperCmds      = make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 5),
        TamperFirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated)
      by DeviceName;
let SvcTampering =
    SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(recentWindow)
    | where EventID in (7034, 7035, 7036, 7040, 7045)
    | where ServiceName has_any (
        "ZscalerService", "ZSATunnel", "ZSAUpdater",
        "MsSense", "SenseSvc", "WdFilter", "AADConnect")
    | summarize
        SvcEvents      = count(),
        SvcNames       = make_set(ServiceName, 10),
        SvcStateChange = make_set(Activity, 5),
        SvcFirstSeen   = min(TimeGenerated)
      by Computer;
SilentHosts
| join kind=leftouter AgentTampering on $left.SourceIP == $right.DeviceName
| join kind=leftouter SvcTampering   on $left.SourceIP == $right.Computer
| extend
    TamperEvents = coalesce(TamperEvents, 0),
    SvcEvents    = coalesce(SvcEvents, 0)
| extend EvasionScore =
    toint(BaselineRequestsPerDay * 2)
  + iff(TamperEvents > 0, 50, 0)
  + iff(SvcEvents    > 0, 40, 0)
| project
    SourceIP, BaselineUsers, BaselineRequestsPerDay,
    TamperEvents, TamperActions, TamperCmds,
    SvcEvents, SvcNames, SvcStateChange,
    EvasionScore,
    TamperFirstSeen, SvcFirstSeen
| order by EvasionScore desc, BaselineRequestsPerDay desc

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: Host {{SourceIP}} went silent in ZIA after averaging {{BaselineRequestsPerDay}} requests/day. Tamper events: {{TamperEvents}} (MDE DeviceEvents), service events: {{SvcEvents}} (Security Log). EvasionScore: {{EvasionScore}}.

properties.displayName: Fortinet UTM Malware and IPS Detection Events
properties.description: Detects FortiGate Unified Threat Management events where antivirus, IPS, anti-bot, file-block or FortiClient UTM inspection blocked or flagged traffic on the gateway. A blocked AV signature means the gateway saw malware on the wire, while a blocked IPS signature means an exploit was attempted against a protected service, and either one can be the first indication of a compromised workstation reaching out to a command server. A single block is rarely conclusive on its own, so start by establishing whether the source was an internal workstation or a server, whether the same signature fires repeatedly from the same host, and whether Defender for Endpoint has already raised a malware alert on that host. The IPS or malware signature is carried in the CEF cs1 field and in the catdesc extension of the raw CEF string, so confirm which of the two the connector populates in the target workspace before relying on the signature column for correlation. MITRE ATT&CK: T1105, T1204.002
properties.query:
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where DeviceEventClassID has_any ("utm", "antivirus")
    or Activity has_any ("ips", "ips-packet", "av", "antibot", "file-block", "fct-utm")
| extend Action = tolower(tostring(DeviceAction))
| extend IsBlocked = Action in ("blocked", "deny", "close", "timeout", "reset")
| extend SeverityHigh = tolower(tostring(LogSeverity)) == "high"
| where IsBlocked or SeverityHigh
| extend UTMType = case(
    Activity has_any ("antibot"), "antibot",
    Activity has_any ("file-block"), "file-block",
    Activity has_any ("ips-packet"), "ips-packet",
    Activity has_any ("ips"), "ips",
    Activity has_any ("antivirus"), "antivirus",
    Activity has_any ("av"), "av",
    Activity has_any ("fct-utm"), "fct-utm",
    "utm")
| extend UTMSignature = iff(
    isnotempty(DeviceCustomString1),
    tostring(DeviceCustomString1),
    tostring(extract(@"catdesc=([^ ]+)", 1, tostring(AdditionalExtensions))))
| extend UTMOutcome = iff(IsBlocked, "Blocked", "Detected")
| summarize
    EventCount     = count(),
    Destinations   = tostring(make_set(DestinationIP, 20)),
    DestPorts      = tostring(make_set(DestinationPort, 10)),
    UserList       = tostring(make_set(SourceUserName, 10)),
    Account        = arg_max(SourceUserName, TimeGenerated),
    Severities     = tostring(make_set(LogSeverity, 5)),
    FortiOSVersion = tostring(make_set(DeviceVersion, 3)),
    Outcomes       = tostring(make_set(UTMOutcome, 5)),
    FirstSeen      = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen       = max(TimeGenerated)
  by SourceIP, UTMType, UTMSignature
| order by EventCount desc

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: FortiGate {{UTMType}} signature {{UTMSignature}} fired {{EventCount}} times from {{SourceIP}} (outcome {{UTMOutcome}}). Users {{UserList}}, destinations {{Destinations}}. Confirm whether the source host is infected or is the victim of an exploit attempt.

properties.displayName: Fortinet Web Filter Blocked Web Access
properties.description: Detects FortiGate web filter events where a page, download or URL was blocked by category or by reputation scoring before reaching the user. Web filtering is one of the most commonly deployed phishing and malware delivery controls on a FortiGate estate, so a block on a newly registered or uncategorised site is a high value early warning that a phishing link or a drive-by download reached an internal user. The benign case is a user browsing a category that the organisation deliberately blocks, such as adult content, gambling or newly observed cloud storage, so check the requested URL, the identity of the user and the configured filter category before escalating to an incident. The web filter category is carried in the CEF cs1 field and in the catdesc extension of the raw CEF string, so confirm which of the two the connector populates in the target workspace before using the category for tuning. MITRE ATT&CK: T1566.002, T1071.001
properties.query:
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where DeviceEventClassID has_any ("webfilter") or Activity has_any ("webfilter", "web-filter")
| where tolower(tostring(DeviceAction)) in ("blocked", "deny", "close", "reset", "timeout")
| extend WebCategory = iff(
    isnotempty(DeviceCustomString1),
    tostring(DeviceCustomString1),
    tostring(extract(@"catdesc=([^ ]+)", 1, tostring(AdditionalExtensions))))
| extend BlockedURL = tostring(RequestURL)
| extend BlockedHost = tostring(DestinationHostName)
| summarize
    BlockCount   = count(),
    Categories   = tostring(make_set(WebCategory, 10)),
    CategoryList = tostring(make_set(WebCategory, 10)),
    UserList     = tostring(make_set(SourceUserName, 10)),
    Account      = arg_max(SourceUserName, TimeGenerated),
    URLList      = tostring(make_set(BlockedURL, 5)),
    MatchedURL   = arg_max(BlockedURL, TimeGenerated),
    HostList     = tostring(make_set(BlockedHost, 10)),
    Destinations = tostring(make_set(DestinationIP, 10)),
    FirstSeen    = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen     = max(TimeGenerated)
  by SourceIP, WebCategory
| order by BlockCount desc

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: Web filter blocked {{BlockCount}} requests from {{SourceIP}} in category {{WebCategory}}. User(s) {{UserList}}, URLs {{URLList}}, hosts {{HostList}}. Review for phishing links or drive-by downloads reaching internal users.

properties.displayName: Fortinet DNS Anomaly - Tunnelling, High Volume and NXDOMAIN Flooding
properties.description: Detects anomalous FortiGate DNS activity from a single internal source host across three independent shapes: an abnormally high query volume in a fifteen minute window, an over-long or deeply nested DNS name with a long single label which is the signature of dnscat2, iodine or dns2tcp tunnelling, and a high ratio of NXDOMAIN answers which indicates domain generation algorithm or DNS bombing behaviour. A DNS tunnel is a low and slow exfiltration channel that most perimeter controls miss because every query is a valid HTTPS or DNS session on the wire, so the firewall DNS log is often the only place it becomes visible. The benign case is a software update client, a container registry or a security product that legitimately resolves thousands of names, so check the queried hostnames, the resolved DNS server and whether the same host shows a matching pattern in proxy logs before escalating. The NXDOMAIN ratio is derived from the rcode extension of the raw CEF string, so confirm the connector populates the rcode extension in the target workspace. MITRE ATT&CK: T1071.004, T1562.001
properties.query:
let HighVolumeThreshold = 300;
let TunnelQueryThreshold = 20;
let LongHostLength = 100;
let LongLabelLength = 30;
let DeepChainDepth = 5;
let NxDomainRatio = 0.80;
let DnsVolume =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(15m)
    | where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
    | where DeviceEventClassID has_any ("dns") or Activity has_any ("dns")
    | where isnotempty(DestinationHostName)
    | extend
        HostLength = strlen(DestinationHostName),
        LabelDepth = countof(DestinationHostName, "."),
        RCode      = extract(@"rcode=(\d+)", 1, tostring(AdditionalExtensions)),
        IsNxDomain = tolower(tostring(RCode)) == "3"
    | summarize
        QueryCount    = count(),
        UniqueHosts   = dcount(DestinationHostName),
        MaxHostLength = max(HostLength),
        MaxLabelDepth = max(LabelDepth),
        NxDomainCount = countif(IsNxDomain),
        LongestHost   = arg_max(DestinationHostName, HostLength),
        SampleHosts   = tostring(make_set(DestinationHostName, 5)),
        DestServers   = tostring(make_set(DestinationIP, 5)),
        FirstSeen     = min(TimeGenerated),
        LastSeen      = max(TimeGenerated)
      by SourceIP;
let DnsLabelShape =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(15m)
    | where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
    | where DeviceEventClassID has_any ("dns") or Activity has_any ("dns")
    | where isnotempty(DestinationHostName)
    | extend Labels = split(DestinationHostName, ".")
    | mv-expand Label = Labels
    | extend LabelLength = strlen(Label)
    | summarize
        MaxLabelLength = max(LabelLength),
        UniqueLabels   = dcount(Label)
      by SourceIP;
DnsVolume
| join kind=leftouter DnsLabelShape on $left.SourceIP == $right.SourceIP
| extend MaxLabelLength = iff(isempty(MaxLabelLength), 0, MaxLabelLength)
| extend NxRatio = iff(QueryCount > 0, round(toreal(NxDomainCount) / toreal(QueryCount), 2), 0.0)
| extend IsHighVolume = QueryCount >= HighVolumeThreshold
| extend IsLongHost = MaxHostLength >= LongHostLength
| extend IsLongLabel = MaxLabelLength >= LongLabelLength
| extend IsDeepChain = MaxLabelDepth >= DeepChainDepth
| extend IsHighNxRatio = NxRatio >= NxDomainRatio
| where IsHighVolume or IsLongHost or IsLongLabel or IsDeepChain or IsHighNxRatio
| extend AnomalyType = case(
    IsLongLabel and QueryCount >= TunnelQueryThreshold, "DNS Tunnelling - Encoded Payload Label",
    IsLongHost, "DNS Tunnelling - Over Long FQDN",
    IsDeepChain, "DNS Tunnelling - Deep Subdomain Chain",
    IsHighNxRatio and IsHighVolume, "DGA or DNS Flooding - High NXDOMAIN Ratio",
    IsHighNxRatio, "Abnormal NXDOMAIN Ratio",
    IsHighVolume, "Abnormal DNS Query Volume",
    "DNS Anomaly")
| order by QueryCount desc, MaxLabelLength desc

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: Source {{SourceIP}} produced {{QueryCount}} DNS queries ({{UniqueHosts}} unique names, max label {{MaxLabelLength}} chars, max depth {{MaxLabelDepth}}, NXDOMAIN ratio {{NxRatio}}) classified as {{AnomalyType}}. Sample names: {{SampleHosts}}. Check for DNS tunnelling or DGA traffic.

properties.displayName: Fortinet Application Control Block of High Risk Application
properties.description: Detects FortiGate application control blocks where the application or the application category belongs to a high risk family: peer to peer and torrent clients, proxy and anonymiser tools, cloud storage and consumer file sharing services, and unauthorised remote access or tunnelling utilities. Application control is the control that stops a user dragging data out of the organisation through an unsanctioned channel, so a block in one of these categories is a direct exfiltration or policy bypass attempt rather than a generic web browsing event. The benign case is a user whose work genuinely requires the blocked application, for example a designer using a specific cloud drive, so confirm the business justification and whether the application was explicitly allowed for that user group before closing the alert. The application name is carried in the app field and the application category in the CEF cs1 field or the appcat extension of the raw CEF string, so confirm which of the two the connector populates in the target workspace. MITRE ATT&CK: T1048, T1090
properties.query:
let RiskAppTerms = dynamic([
    "p2p", "torrent", "bittorrent", "proxy", "socks", "anonymiz", "anonymis",
    "psiphon", "onion", "dropbox", "onedrive", "drive.google", "icloud",
    "box.com", "mega", "wetransfer", "pastebin", "filezilla", "anydesk",
    "teamviewer", "zerotier", "tailscale", "openvpn", "softether"]);
let RiskCategoryTerms = dynamic([
    "p2p", "peer-to-peer", "torrent", "proxy", "anonymiz", "anonymis",
    "vpn", "cloud", "tunnel", "remote.admin"]);
let BlockActions = dynamic(["deny", "blocked", "close", "reset", "timeout"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(15m)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where DeviceEventClassID has_any ("app-ctrl", "appctrl") or Activity has_any ("appctrl", "app-ctrl", "app-control")
| extend AppName = tostring(ApplicationProtocol)
| extend AppCategory = iff(
    isnotempty(DeviceCustomString1),
    tostring(DeviceCustomString1),
    tostring(extract(@"appcat=([^ ]+)", 1, tostring(AdditionalExtensions))))
| where AppName has_any (RiskAppTerms) or AppCategory has_any (RiskCategoryTerms)
| where tolower(tostring(DeviceAction)) in (BlockActions)
| extend RiskClass = case(
    AppName has_any ("p2p", "torrent", "bittorrent") or AppCategory has_any ("p2p", "peer-to-peer", "torrent"), "Peer to Peer or Torrent",
    AppName has_any ("proxy", "socks", "anonymiz", "anonymis", "psiphon", "onion") or AppCategory has_any ("proxy", "anonymiz", "anonymis"), "Proxy or Anonymiser",
    AppName has_any ("dropbox", "onedrive", "drive.google", "icloud", "box.com", "mega", "wetransfer", "pastebin") or AppCategory has_any ("cloud"), "Cloud Storage or File Sharing",
    AppName has_any ("openvpn", "softether", "anydesk", "teamviewer", "zerotier", "tailscale", "filezilla") or AppCategory has_any ("vpn", "tunnel", "remote.admin"), "Unauthorised Remote Access or Tunnel",
    "Risky Application Category")
| summarize
    BlockCount    = count(),
    AppNames      = tostring(make_set(AppName, 10)),
    AppCategories = tostring(make_set(AppCategory, 10)),
    Users         = tostring(make_set(SourceUserName, 10)),
    Account       = arg_max(SourceUserName, TimeGenerated),
    Destinations  = tostring(make_set(DestinationIP, 10)),
    SampleURLs    = tostring(make_set(RequestURL, 5)),
    BytesSent     = sum(SentBytes),
    FirstSeen     = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen      = max(TimeGenerated)
  by SourceIP, RiskClass
| extend TotalMBSent = round(toreal(BytesSent) / 1048576, 2)
| order by BlockCount desc, TotalMBSent desc

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: Application control blocked {{BlockCount}} sessions from {{SourceIP}} in risk class {{RiskClass}}. Applications {{AppNames}}, user(s) {{Users}}, {{TotalMBSent}} MB sent, destinations {{Destinations}}. Review for unsanctioned exfiltration or policy bypass.

properties.displayName: Fortinet SSL-VPN Successful Logon Anomaly
properties.description: Detects successful FortiGate SSL-VPN logons that do not fit the established pattern for the source address, the time of day or the number of identities involved. The rule raises an alert when a source IP has never been seen connecting through the VPN before, when the logon happens outside business hours, or when a single source address authenticates many distinct users in the same window. A first seen source is the highest value signal here, because a valid credential used from a new network is exactly what a stolen VPN account looks like, and many distinct users behind one address is the classic shape of credential stuffing or a shared or proxied exit node. The benign case is a staff member or an approved contractor connecting from a new home network or a new mobile carrier address, so check the source address reputation and confirm the user travel before escalating. The historical baseline for the first seen test is a thirty day lookback over the same VPN log categories, so a source that has been in use for longer than thirty days will not raise the first seen condition. MITRE ATT&CK: T1078, T1078.002
properties.query:
let DistinctUserThreshold = 5;
let BusinessStartHour = 7;
let BusinessEndHour = 19;
// 30 day baseline used to decide whether a source IP has been seen on the VPN before.
let KnownVpnSources =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
    | where DeviceEventClassID has_any ("sslvpn", "vpn") or Activity has_any ("sslvpn", "ssl-vpn", "vpn")
    | where isnotempty(SourceIP)
    | summarize HistFirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), HistLastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by SourceIP;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where DeviceEventClassID has_any ("sslvpn", "vpn") or Activity has_any ("sslvpn", "ssl-vpn", "vpn")
| where tolower(tostring(DeviceAction)) in ("accept", "close", "success", "allow", "login")
    or EventOutcome == "Success"
| where isnotempty(SourceIP)
| extend LogonHour = hour(TimeGenerated)
| extend IsOffHours = LogonHour < BusinessStartHour or LogonHour >= BusinessEndHour
| summarize
    LogonCount    = count(),
    DistinctUsers = dcount(SourceUserName),
    UserList      = tostring(make_set(SourceUserName, 20)),
    Account       = arg_max(SourceUserName, TimeGenerated),
    OffHoursCount = countif(IsOffHours),
    LogonHours    = tostring(make_set(LogonHour, 12)),
    Destinations  = tostring(make_set(DestinationIP, 10)),
    FirstSeen     = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen      = max(TimeGenerated)
  by SourceIP
| join kind=leftouter KnownVpnSources on $left.SourceIP == $right.SourceIP
| extend IsFirstSeenSource = isempty(HistFirstSeen)
| where IsFirstSeenSource or OffHoursCount > 0 or DistinctUsers >= DistinctUserThreshold
| extend AnomalyType = case(
    IsFirstSeenSource and DistinctUsers >= DistinctUserThreshold, "New source IP authenticating many distinct users",
    IsFirstSeenSource and OffHoursCount > 0, "New source IP with off hours logon",
    DistinctUsers >= DistinctUserThreshold, "Many distinct users from a single source IP",
    IsFirstSeenSource, "First observed SSL-VPN source IP",
    "Off hours SSL-VPN logon")
| order by DistinctUsers desc, LogonCount desc

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: SSL-VPN source {{SourceIP}} produced {{LogonCount}} successful logons across {{DistinctUsers}} distinct users ({{OffHoursCount}} outside business hours), classified as {{AnomalyType}}. Users {{UserList}}. Validate whether the account and the source address are legitimate.

properties.displayName: Fortinet Administrative and Configuration Change
properties.description: Detects FortiGate administrative and configuration events, covering administrative logons, configuration and object changes, policy changes and the creation or modification of local, remote, LDAP and RADIUS user accounts. A change made in the FortiGate console or CLI is the single most powerful persistence and defence evasion action available to an attacker who has obtained administrative access, because it can add a new administrator, disable logging, open a firewall policy or weaken a security profile in a single action. The benign case is a change made by a network engineer during a planned maintenance window, so the first check is always the admin identity and whether a change ticket exists for that source address. The message text is used to classify the change because FortiGate does not expose a dedicated subtype for configuration objects, so the rule matches on the human readable message and the event subtype together. MITRE ATT&CK: T1098, T1078
properties.query:
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where DeviceEventClassID has_any ("event") or Activity has_any ("admin-login", "admin", "user", "system", "config", "login")
| extend Msg = tolower(tostring(Message))
| extend Ext = tolower(tostring(AdditionalExtensions))
| extend ChangeKind = case(
    Msg has_any ("user created", "user added", "user deleted", "user modified", "user updated", "password changed", "password set", "group created", "group deleted", "admin created", "admin deleted", "admin updated", "administrator created", "sso user", "ldap user", "radius user", "local user created", "remote user created"), "Account or Credential Change",
    Msg has_any ("config", "configuration") or Ext has_any ("config"), "Configuration Change",
    Msg has_any ("policy", "address group", "service group", "static route", "ipsec phase") or Ext has_any ("policy"), "Policy or Object Change",
    Activity has_any ("admin-login"), "Administrative Login",
    Msg has_any ("disabled", "disable", "enabled", "changed", "updated", "modified", "created", "deleted", "added", "removed", "upgraded", "imported", "exported", "stopped", "restarted"), "System or Setting Change",
    "Other Administrative Event")
| where ChangeKind != "Other Administrative Event"
| summarize
    EventCount  = count(),
    Admins      = tostring(make_set(SourceUserName, 10)),
    Account     = arg_max(SourceUserName, TimeGenerated),
    MessageList = tostring(make_set(Message, 5)),
    Actions     = tostring(make_set(DeviceAction, 5)),
    Activities  = tostring(make_set(Activity, 10)),
    Severities  = tostring(make_set(LogSeverity, 5)),
    FortiOS     = tostring(make_set(DeviceVersion, 3)),
    FirstSeen   = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen    = max(TimeGenerated)
  by ChangeKind, SourceIP
| order by ChangeKind asc, EventCount desc

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: {{ChangeKind}} performed from {{SourceIP}} by admin {{Admins}} ({{EventCount}} events). Messages {{MessageList}}. Verify the change against an approved change ticket and confirm the admin identity.

properties.displayName: Fortinet VPN Tunnel Traffic Pivoting to Internal Destinations
properties.description: Detects FortiGate traffic sessions where the source address sits on the internet facing side of the tunnel while the destination is an internal RFC1918 address, which is the signature of remote access traffic that has been tunnelled in and is now pivoting towards internal servers and workstations. A session that lands on an administrative or file sharing port on an internal host is the classic stepping stone for lateral movement once a VPN account has been stolen or sold on. The benign case is a legitimate remote worker reaching an internal application, so check the destination service, the port and whether the source address is a known remote user address before treating the session as a pivot. The rule deliberately requires either more than one distinct internal destination or a sensitive destination port so that a single published DMZ service does not generate a flood of alerts, and the tunnel context fields are only a corroborating signal because the connector may not populate them. MITRE ATT&CK: T1020, T1133
properties.query:
let SensitivePorts = dynamic([
    "22", "445", "135", "139", "3389", "5985", "5986", "1433", "3306",
    "8080", "8443", "4648", "4649", "389", "636", "88"]);
let MinDistinctDestinations = 2;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where DeviceEventClassID has_any ("traffic") or Activity has_any ("forward", "local-in")
| where isnotempty(SourceIP) and isnotempty(DestinationIP)
| where ipv4_is_valid(SourceIP) and ipv4_is_valid(DestinationIP)
| where ipv4_is_private(SourceIP) == false
| where ipv4_is_private(DestinationIP) == true
| extend DestPort = tostring(DestinationPort)
| extend IsSensitivePort = DestPort in (SensitivePorts)
| extend TunnelContext = Activity has_any ("vpn", "sslvpn", "ssl-vpn", "tunnel", "ipsec")
    or tostring(AdditionalExtensions) has_any ("tunnelip", "remip", "tunneltype", "vpnuser", "vpn")
| summarize
    SessionCount     = count(),
    Destinations     = tostring(make_set(DestinationIP, 20)),
    DistinctDests    = dcount(DestinationIP),
    DestPorts        = tostring(make_set(DestinationPort, 10)),
    SensitivePortHit = countif(IsSensitivePort),
    TunnelContextHit = countif(TunnelContext),
    AppProtocols     = tostring(make_set(ApplicationProtocol, 10)),
    Users            = tostring(make_set(SourceUserName, 10)),
    Account          = arg_max(SourceUserName, TimeGenerated),
    TotalBytesSent   = sum(SentBytes),
    TotalBytesRecv   = sum(ReceivedBytes),
    Actions          = tostring(make_set(DeviceAction, 5)),
    FirstSeen        = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen         = max(TimeGenerated)
  by SourceIP
| where DistinctDests >= MinDistinctDestinations or SensitivePortHit > 0
| order by SensitivePortHit desc, DistinctDests desc

alertDetailsOverride.alertDisplayNameFormat: Fortinet Tunnel Pivot - {{SourceIP}} to {{DistinctDests}} internal hosts
alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: Internet facing source {{SourceIP}} reached {{DistinctDests}} internal destinations on ports {{DestPorts}} ({{SensitivePortHit}} sensitive port sessions, tunnel context hits {{TunnelContextHit}}). Users {{Users}}, {{TotalBytesSent}} bytes sent. Review for lateral movement over a stolen VPN session.

properties.displayName: Fortinet Traffic, IPS and Botnet Anomaly Events
properties.description: Detects FortiGate anomaly events, covering the forward traffic anomaly, IPS anomaly, AV anomaly, flood and denial of service subtypes that the gateway raises when session behaviour departs from the configured profile, and it surfaces the same class of events that a botnet signature produces. FortiGate anomaly logging is one of the cheapest ways to see volumetric abuse that never forms a single recognisable pattern, such as a slow SYN flood, an HTTP flood or a command and control burst from an infected host, and it is often the only place the volume is visible because each individual session looks legitimate. The benign case is a genuine capacity event such as a large legitimate download, a backup window or a software update, so compare the byte totals against known business activity and check whether the source is an internal or an external address. The rule groups on the source and destination pair and requires a small minimum number of anomaly events or a large byte total so that a single misclassified session does not become an alert. MITRE ATT&CK: T1498, T1499
properties.query:
let AnomalyEventThreshold = 3;
let HighByteThreshold = 1073741824;
let AnomalySubTypes = dynamic([
    "forward-anomaly", "ips-anomaly", "av-anomaly", "flood-anomaly",
    "dos-anomaly", "botnet", "anomaly"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where Activity has_any (AnomalySubTypes)
    or DeviceEventClassID has_any ("anomaly")
    or tolower(tostring(Message)) has_any ("anomaly", "flood", "botnet", "denial of service")
| extend AnomalyType = case(
    Activity has_any ("forward-anomaly"), "Forward Traffic Anomaly",
    Activity has_any ("ips-anomaly"), "IPS Anomaly",
    Activity has_any ("av-anomaly"), "AV Anomaly",

properties.displayName: Fortinet DLP Sensitive Data Pattern Match
properties.description: Detects FortiGate data loss prevention events where a sensitive data pattern matched in the inspected content, which is a direct confirmation that regulated or confidential data was present in the traffic that the gateway just inspected. Depending on the DLP profile the action may have been a block, a redaction or a detect only event, so the outcome is reported alongside the pattern to separate a stopped transfer from one that was allowed through. The benign case is a legitimate business transfer that a DLP rule over matches, for example a supplier invoice containing a tax identifier, so check the matched pattern, the user and the destination before escalating. The matched pattern name is carried in the CEF cs1 field and in the pattern extension of the raw CEF string, and the profile and action in the profile and action extensions, so confirm which of these the connector populates in the target workspace before relying on the pattern column for triage. If neither the cs1 field nor the pattern extension is available the rule falls back to the DLP event itself and reports the pattern class as Other DLP Pattern. MITRE ATT&CK: T1041
properties.query:
let SensitivePatternTerms = dynamic([
    "ssn", "social security", "credit card", "card number", "cardholder", "cvv", "cvc2",
    "bank account", "iban", "swift code", "passport", "national id", "tax id",
    "medical record", "health record", "patient", "diagnosis", "prescription",
    "invoice", "payroll", "salary", "financial statement", "account balance",
    "confidential", "proprietary", "source code", "api key", "licence key", "license key",
    "password", "credential", "pci-dss", "hipaa", "pii", "gdpr"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where DeviceEventClassID has_any ("dlp") or Activity has_any ("dlp")
| extend DLPPattern = iff(
    isnotempty(DeviceCustomString1),
    tostring(DeviceCustomString1),
    tostring(extract(@"pattern=([^ ]+)", 1, tostring(AdditionalExtensions))))
| extend DLPAction = tostring(extract(@"action=([^ ]+)", 1, tostring(AdditionalExtensions)))
| extend DLPProfile = tostring(extract(@"profile=([^ ]+)", 1, tostring(AdditionalExtensions)))
| where isnotempty(DLPPattern)
    or tolower(tostring(Message)) has_any ("dlp", "sensitive", "pattern")
| extend PatternClass = case(
    DLPPattern has_any (SensitivePatternTerms) or tostring(Message) has_any (SensitivePatternTerms), "Sensitive Data Pattern",
    "Other DLP Pattern")
| extend DLPOutcome = case(
    tolower(tostring(DeviceAction)) in ("block", "blocked", "deny", "close", "redact", "quarantine"), "Blocked or Redacted",
    tolower(tostring(DLPAction)) has_any ("block", "redact", "deny"), "Blocked or Redacted",
    tolower(tostring(DeviceAction)) in ("allow", "accept"), "Allowed - Detected Only",
    "Detected")
| summarize
    MatchCount   = count(),
    PatternList  = tostring(make_set(DLPPattern, 10)),
    Outcomes     = tostring(make_set(DLPOutcome, 5)),
    Profiles     = tostring(make_set(DLPProfile, 5)),
    Users        = tostring(make_set(SourceUserName, 10)),
    Account      = arg_max(SourceUserName, TimeGenerated),
    Destinations = tostring(make_set(DestinationIP, 10)),
    DataURL      = tostring(make_set(RequestURL, 5)),
    BytesSent    = sum(SentBytes),
    FirstSeen    = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen     = max(TimeGenerated)
  by SourceIP, PatternClass, DLPOutcome
| order by MatchCount desc

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: DLP raised {{MatchCount}} sensitive data matches from {{SourceIP}} classified as {{PatternClass}} with outcome {{DLPOutcome}}. User {{Users}}, pattern {{PatternList}}, destinations {{Destinations}}. Confirm whether the transfer was authorised.

properties.displayName: Fortinet Logging or Security Control Disabled
properties.description: Detects FortiGate events that indicate logging or a security control was switched off, which covers the log service being stopped, an administrator disabling a log setting such as event, traffic or sniffer logging, and an administrator disabling a protective control such as admin access, SSH, HTTPS, IPsec, DNS, web filtering, IPS or antivirus. An attacker who reaches the FortiGate console will frequently silence the logging first, because an unlogged control change removes the evidence of everything that follows, so this detection is about the defender's visibility rather than about the change itself. The benign case is a planned maintenance action where an engineer temporarily disables a feature, so always check the admin identity and the change record before treating the event as malicious. The rule deliberately requires a high severity event subtype, because FortiGate marks log and control tampering as a critical or high event, and the message text is used to confirm the intent because the subtype alone does not distinguish a change from a routine administrative logon. MITRE ATT&CK: T1562.001, T1562.008
properties.query:
let ControlDisableTerms = dynamic([
    "log service", "logs stopped", "log stopped", "stopped logging", "logging stopped",
    "log disabled", "disable log", "disable logging", "disabled logging", "log setting",
    "event log", "traffic log", "sniffer", "syslog",
    "disable admin", "admin disabled", "disabled admin",
    "disable ssh", "disable https", "disable telnet", "disable ipsec", "disable ssl",
    "disable dns", "disable webfilter", "disable ips", "disable antivirus",
    "disable forticloud", "disable fortiguard", "disable all", "disable local-in",
    "disable console", "disable gui", "bypass", "tamper"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(6h)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where DeviceEventClassID has_any ("event") or Activity has_any ("system", "admin", "config", "admin-login")
| where tolower(tostring(LogSeverity)) == "high"
| extend Msg = tolower(tostring(Message))
| extend Ext = tolower(tostring(AdditionalExtensions))
| where Msg has_any (ControlDisableTerms) or Ext has_any (ControlDisableTerms)
| extend ControlType = case(
    Msg has_any ("log service", "logs stopped", "log stopped", "stopped logging", "logging stopped", "log disabled", "disable log", "disable logging", "disabled logging", "log setting", "event log", "traffic log", "sniffer", "syslog"), "Logging Service or Setting Disabled",
    Msg has_any ("disable admin", "admin disabled", "disabled admin", "disable ssh", "disable https", "disable telnet", "disable ipsec", "disable ssl", "disable dns", "disable webfilter", "disable ips", "disable antivirus", "disable forticloud", "disable fortiguard", "disable all", "disable local-in", "disable console", "disable gui"), "Security Control Disabled",
    Msg has_any ("bypass", "tamper"), "Control Bypass or Tamper",
    "High Severity System or Admin Event")
| summarize
    EventCount  = count(),
    Admins      = tostring(make_set(SourceUserName, 10)),
    Account     = arg_max(SourceUserName, TimeGenerated),
    Messages    = tostring(make_set(Message, 5)),
    Activities  = tostring(make_set(Activity, 10)),
    Actions     = tostring(make_set(DeviceAction, 5)),
    FortiOS     = tostring(make_set(DeviceVersion, 3)),
    FirstSeen   = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen    = max(TimeGenerated)
  by ControlType, SourceIP
| order by EventCount desc

alertDetailsOverride.alertDescriptionFormat: FortiGate recorded {{EventCount}} high severity event(s) of type {{ControlType}} from {{SourceIP}}. Admin {{Admins}}. Messages {{Messages}}. Confirm whether a legitimate maintenance window authorised the change, otherwise assume visibility has been reduced deliberately.

properties.displayName: CSL Hunt Q01 - Beaconing Detection - All Vendors
properties.query:
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DeviceVendor in ("Fortinet", "Palo Alto Networks", "Zscaler")
| where tolower(DeviceAction) in ("accept", "allowed", "allow")
| where isnotempty(SourceIP) and isnotempty(DestinationIP)
| where ipv4_is_private(SourceIP) == true
| where ipv4_is_private(DestinationIP) == false
| where not(ipv4_is_in_range(DestinationIP, "100.64.0.0/10"))
| where not(ipv4_is_in_range(DestinationIP, "169.254.0.0/16"))
| where not(ipv4_is_in_range(DestinationIP, "224.0.0.0/4"))
| summarize
    ConnectionCount  = count(),
    BytesSent        = sum(SentBytes),
    BytesReceived    = sum(ReceivedBytes),
    HourlyBuckets    = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)),
    ActiveMinutes    = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)),
    Ports            = make_set(DestinationPort, 10),
    FirstSeen        = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen         = max(TimeGenerated)
  by SourceIP, DestinationIP, DeviceVendor
| where ConnectionCount > 20 and HourlyBuckets >= 3
| extend BeaconScore = round(toreal(ConnectionCount) / toreal(HourlyBuckets), 1)
| where BeaconScore > 5
| order by BeaconScore desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Detects internal hosts making regular high-frequency connections to the same external IP across multiple hours. Beacon score = connections / hourly buckets.

properties.displayName: CSL Hunt Q02 - Data Exfiltration - Anomalous Outbound Volume

| where isnotempty(SourceIP) and isnotempty(DestinationIP)
| where ipv4_is_private(SourceIP) == true

    TotalBytesSent    = sum(SentBytes),

    | where DestinationHostName has_any (ExfilDomains)
    | summarize
        DaySentBytes    = sum(SentBytes),
        DayRequestCount = count(),
        DayDestinCount  = dcount(DestinationHostName)
      by UserName = tolower(SourceUserName), Day = bin(TimeGenerated, 1d);
let ZIA_Users =
    ZIA_Daily
    | summarize
        ZIA_TotalMBSent   = round(toreal(sum(DaySentBytes)) / 1048576, 2),
        ZIA_ActiveDays    = dcount(Day),
        ZIA_TotalRequests = sum(DayRequestCount),
        ZIA_UniqueDestCnt = sum(DayDestinCount)
      by UserName;
let globalAvg = toscalar(ZIA_Users | summarize avg(ZIA_TotalMBSent));
let globalStd = toscalar(ZIA_Users | summarize stdev(ZIA_TotalMBSent));
let O365_Sharing =
    OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(HuntWindow)
    | where isnotempty(UserId)
    | where Operation in (
        "FileDownloaded", "FileSyncDownloadedFull", "FileCopied",
        "AnonymousLinkCreated", "AnonymousLinkUsed",
        "SharingSet", "SharingInvitationCreated",
        "AddedToSecureLink", "SecureLinkUsed")
    | summarize
        O365_EventCount = count(),
        O365_Operations = make_set(Operation, 10),
        O365_AnonLinks  = countif(Operation has "Anonymous"),
        O365_LastEvent  = max(TimeGenerated)
      by UserName = tolower(UserId);
ZIA_Users
| join kind=leftouter O365_Sharing on UserName
| extend
    O365_EventCount = coalesce(O365_EventCount, 0),
    O365_AnonLinks  = coalesce(O365_AnonLinks, 0)
| extend
    Zscore = iff(globalStd > 0,
                 round((ZIA_TotalMBSent - globalAvg) / globalStd, 2),
                 0.0),
    DistinctChannels = iff(ZIA_TotalMBSent > 5, 1, 0)
                     + iff(O365_EventCount  > 0, 1, 0)
| where Zscore >= 3.0
    or (O365_AnonLinks  >= 3 and ZIA_TotalMBSent > 10)
    or (ZIA_ActiveDays  >= 20 and ZIA_TotalMBSent > 50)
| project
    UserName,
    ZIA_TotalMBSent, ZIA_ActiveDays, ZIA_TotalRequests, ZIA_UniqueDestCnt,
    O365_EventCount, O365_AnonLinks, O365_Operations,
    DistinctChannels, Zscore
| order by Zscore desc, ZIA_TotalMBSent desc

properties.displayName: CSL Hunt Q30 - Perfect Impostor - Account Takeover in Normal Traffic
properties.query:
let baselineWindow = 14d;
let recentWindow   = 4h;
let ZPA_Baseline =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(baselineWindow) .. ago(recentWindow))
    | where DeviceVendor == "Zscaler" and DeviceProduct has "ZPA"
    | where DeviceAction !in ("block", "BLOCK", "Failed")
    | where isnotempty(SourceUserName)
    | extend BaselineCountry = tostring(geo_info_from_ip_address(SourceIP).country)
    | summarize
        BaselineCountries = make_set(BaselineCountry, 20),
        BaselineAppCount  = dcount(DestinationHostName)
      by UserName = tolower(SourceUserName);
let ZPA_Recent =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(recentWindow)
    | where DeviceVendor == "Zscaler" and DeviceProduct has "ZPA"
    | where isnotempty(SourceUserName)
    | extend RecentCountry = tostring(geo_info_from_ip_address(SourceIP).country)
    | summarize
        RecentCountries = make_set(RecentCountry, 5),
        RecentApps      = make_set(DestinationHostName, 10),
        RecentIPs       = make_set(SourceIP, 5),
        RecentConnCount = count(),
        ZPA_FirstSeen   = min(TimeGenerated)
      by UserName = tolower(SourceUserName);
let ZIA_Suspicious =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(recentWindow)
    | where DeviceVendor == "Zscaler"
    | where isnotempty(SourceUserName)
    | where DeviceCustomString2 has_any (
        "REMOTE_ACCESS_TOOLS", "REMOTE_ADMINISTRATION", "WEB_BASED_ADMIN",
        "ACCOUNT_CREATION", "TUNNEL_SOCKS_PROXY", "ANONYMOUS_PROXY",
        "ONLINE_STORAGE", "FILE_SHARE", "TOR", "VPN_SERVICES",
        "NEWLY_REGISTERED_DOMAINS", "PHISHING")
    | summarize
        ZIA_Categories   = make_set(DeviceCustomString2, 10),
        ZIA_Destinations = make_set(DestinationHostName, 10),
        ZIA_RequestCount = count(),
        ZIA_FirstSeen    = min(TimeGenerated)
      by UserName = tolower(SourceUserName);
let IdP_Changes =
    OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(recentWindow)
    | where isnotempty(UserId)
    | where Operation in (
        "New-InboxRule",                         // auto-forward / hide rules
        "Set-Mailbox",                           // mailbox delegation
        "Add-MailboxPermission",
        "Add OAuth2PermissionGrant",             // OAuth consent grant
        "Consent to application",
        "Add service principal credentials",
        "Update user",
        "Disable Strong Authentication",         // MFA removal
        "Update StsRefreshTokenValidFrom",       // token invalidation
        "Add member to role")                    // privilege escalation
    | summarize
        IdP_EventCount = count(),
        IdP_Operations = make_set(Operation, 10),
        IdP_FirstSeen  = min(TimeGenerated)
      by UserName = tolower(UserId);
ZPA_Recent
| join kind=inner ZPA_Baseline on UserName
| extend NewCountries = set_difference(RecentCountries, BaselineCountries)
| join kind=leftouter ZIA_Suspicious on UserName
| join kind=leftouter IdP_Changes on UserName
| extend
    ZIA_RequestCount = coalesce(ZIA_RequestCount, 0),
    IdP_EventCount   = coalesce(IdP_EventCount, 0)
| extend ImpostorScore =
    iff(array_length(NewCountries) > 0, 40, 0)
  + (ZIA_RequestCount * 5)
  + (IdP_EventCount * 30)
| where ImpostorScore >= 40
    or (IdP_EventCount >= 1 and ZIA_RequestCount >= 1)
    or array_length(NewCountries) > 0
| project
    UserName,
    NewCountries, RecentCountries, BaselineCountries,
    RecentApps, RecentIPs, RecentConnCount,
    ZIA_Categories, ZIA_Destinations, ZIA_RequestCount,
    IdP_Operations, IdP_EventCount,
    ImpostorScore,
    ZPA_FirstSeen
| order by ImpostorScore desc

properties.displayName: CSL Hunt Q31 - APT Control Evasion - Degrading Zscaler and EDR Visibility
properties.query:
let baselineWindow            = 7d;
let recentWindow              = 4h;
let minBaselineRequestsPerDay = 10;
let ZIA_BaselineHosts =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(baselineWindow) .. ago(recentWindow))
    | where DeviceVendor == "Zscaler"
    | where isnotempty(SourceIP) and isnotempty(SourceUserName)
    | summarize
        BaselineRequestsPerDay = round(toreal(count()) / (baselineWindow / 1d), 1),
        BaselineUsers          = make_set(SourceUserName, 5)
      by SourceIP
    | where BaselineRequestsPerDay >= minBaselineRequestsPerDay;
let ZIA_RecentActive =
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(recentWindow)
    | where DeviceVendor == "Zscaler"
    | where isnotempty(SourceIP)
    | distinct SourceIP;
let SilentHosts =
    ZIA_BaselineHosts
    | join kind=leftanti ZIA_RecentActive on SourceIP;
let AgentTampering =
    DeviceEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(recentWindow)
    | where ActionType in (
        "ServiceUninstalled", "ServiceStopped", "DriverUnloaded",
        "TamperingAttempt", "AntivirusScanFailed")
      or (ActionType == "ProcessCreated"
          and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (
              "ZscalerApp", "ZSATunnel", "ZSAUpdater", "ZscalerService",
              "sc stop", "sc delete", "net stop", "taskkill"))
    | summarize
        TamperEvents    = count(),
        TamperActions   = make_set(ActionType, 10),
        TamperCmds      = make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 5),
        TamperFirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated)
      by DeviceName;
let SvcTampering =
    SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(recentWindow)
    | where EventID in (7034, 7035, 7036, 7040, 7045)
    | where ServiceName has_any (
        "ZscalerService", "ZSATunnel", "ZSAUpdater",
        "MsSense", "SenseSvc", "WdFilter", "AADConnect")
    | summarize
        SvcEvents      = count(),
        SvcNames       = make_set(ServiceName, 10),
        SvcStateChange = make_set(Activity, 5),
        SvcFirstSeen   = min(TimeGenerated)
      by Computer;
SilentHosts
| join kind=leftouter AgentTampering on $left.SourceIP == $right.DeviceName
| join kind=leftouter SvcTampering   on $left.SourceIP == $right.Computer
| extend
    TamperEvents = coalesce(TamperEvents, 0),
    SvcEvents    = coalesce(SvcEvents, 0)
| extend EvasionScore =
    toint(BaselineRequestsPerDay * 2)
  + iff(TamperEvents > 0, 50, 0)
  + iff(SvcEvents    > 0, 40, 0)
| project
    SourceIP, BaselineUsers, BaselineRequestsPerDay,
    TamperEvents, TamperActions, TamperCmds,
    SvcEvents, SvcNames, SvcStateChange,
    EvasionScore,
    TamperFirstSeen, SvcFirstSeen
| order by EvasionScore desc, BaselineRequestsPerDay desc

properties.displayName: CSL Hunt FQ01 - FortiGate Log Coverage Census
properties.query:
let lookback = 24h;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| extend Category = tolower(tostring(DeviceEventClassID))
| extend Subtype  = tolower(tostring(Activity))
| extend LogType   = iff(isempty(Category), "unknown", Category)
| summarize
    EventCount   = count(),
    Subtypes     = make_set(Subtype, 10),
    Actions      = make_set(DeviceAction, 5),

tags.name: description
tags.value: Shows which FortiGate log categories and subtypes are actually arriving in the workspace, with volume and the newest event per category. Run this first. A FortiGate that forwards only "traffic" logs will return nothing for every UTM, VPN, admin, DNS and DLP query in this pack, and that silence looks exactly like a clean perimeter.

properties.displayName: CSL Hunt FQ02 - FortiGate UTM and IPS Signature Leaderboard
properties.query:
let lookback = 24h;
let minHits = 1;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where tolower(DeviceEventClassID) in ("utm", "antivirus", "webfilter", "app-ctrl")
    or tolower(Activity) in ("ips", "ips-packet", "av", "antibot", "file-block",
                             "appctrl", "webfilter", "fct-utm", "ips-anomaly",
                             "av-anomaly")
| extend IPSSignature = iff(isnotempty(DeviceCustomString1),
                            tostring(DeviceCustomString1),
                            extract(@"catdesc=([^ ]+)", 1, tostring(AdditionalExtensions)))
| extend IPSSignature = iff(isempty(IPSSignature), tostring(Activity), IPSSignature)
| summarize
    HitCount        = count(),
    BlockedCount    = countif(tolower(DeviceAction) == "blocked"),
    DetectedCount   = countif(tolower(DeviceAction) == "accept"),
    SourceIPs       = make_set(SourceIP, 20),
    DestHostNames   = make_set(DestinationHostName, 10),
    RequestURLs     = make_set(RequestURL, 10),
    Severities      = make_set(LogSeverity, 5),
    Apps            = make_set(ApplicationProtocol, 5),
    FirstSeen       = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen        = max(TimeGenerated)
  by IPSSignature
| where HitCount > minHits
| extend Enforcement = iff(BlockedCount == 0, "Detected but NOT blocked",
                      iff(DetectedCount == 0, "Blocked", "Mixed"))
| order by HitCount desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Top FortiGate UTM signatures by volume, with the sources that triggered them and the enforcement split. The signature name comes from DeviceCustomString1 where the connector populates it and is otherwise recovered from catdesc in AdditionalExtensions. A signature that is firing constantly is either a real campaign or a detection that is mis-tuned and has trained the analysts to ignore it.

This is the highest-value FortiGate hunt in the pack and is usually a configuration finding rather than an attack.

properties.displayName: CSL Hunt FQ04 - FortiGate SSL-VPN and Admin Successful Logons

    "0102000012",  // local user login success
    "0101001013",  // SSL-VPN tunnel up
    "0101001057"]);// SSL-VPN login

    "admin", "admin-login", "login", "user", "auth", "sslvpn", "ssl-vpn",

Successful logons to the management plane are the ones that matter: an admin console session is full control of the perimeter. tags.name: description
tags.value: FortiGate administrative events - admin logins, configuration changes, account and policy changes. An attacker who reaches the admin console does not have to attack the estate; they change the estate. This hunt is the audit trail for who changed the firewall and from where.

properties.displayName: CSL Hunt FQ07 - FortiGate Web Filter Category Breakdown
properties.query:
let lookback = 7d;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where tolower(DeviceEventClassID) == "webfilter" or tolower(Activity) == "webfilter"
| extend WebCategory = extract(@"catdesc=([^ ]+)", 1, tostring(AdditionalExtensions))
| extend WebCategory = iff(isempty(WebCategory), "unclassified", WebCategory)
| extend Action      = tolower(tostring(DeviceAction))
| summarize
    HitCount       = count(),
    BlockedCount   = countif(Action == "blocked"),
    AllowedCount   = countif(Action == "accept"),

    RequestURLs    = make_set(RequestURL, 10),
    FirstSeen      = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen       = max(TimeGenerated)
  by WebCategory
| extend BlockRate = iff(HitCount > 0, round(100.0 * toreal(BlockedCount) / toreal(HitCount), 1), 0.0)
| order by HitCount desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: What the FortiGate web filter is seeing and deciding, split by category and action. The permitted categories are the interesting column: a category that should be blocked but is being allowed is a control gap, and a category that is constantly allowed to a large volume of traffic is either shadow IT or a misconfiguration.

properties.displayName: CSL Hunt FQ08 - FortiGate DNS Telemetry and Tunneling Indicators
properties.query:
let lookback = 24h;
let minQueries = 500;
let longNameChars = 40;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where tolower(DeviceEventClassID) == "dns" or tolower(Activity) == "dns"
| extend QueriedName = tostring(DestinationHostName)
| extend QueriedName = iff(isempty(QueriedName),
                           extract(@"hostname=([^ ]+)", 1, tostring(AdditionalExtensions)),
                           QueriedName)
| extend ResponseCode = extract(@"rcode=([^ ]+)", 1, tostring(AdditionalExtensions))
| extend NameLength  = strlen(QueriedName)
| summarize
    QueryCount      = count(),
    UniqueNames     = dcount(QueriedName),
    MaxNameLength   = max(NameLength),
    LongNameCount   = countif(NameLength > longNameChars),
    NXDOMAINCount   = countif(ResponseCode has_any ("3", "NXDOMAIN")),
    SourceIPs       = make_set(SourceIP, 20),
    SampleNames     = make_set(QueriedName, 10),
    FirstSeen       = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen        = max(TimeGenerated)
  by SourceIP
| where QueryCount > minQueries
| extend NXDOMAINRatio = iff(QueryCount > 0, round(100.0 * toreal(NXDOMAINCount) / toreal(QueryCount), 1), 0.0)
| extend LongNameRatio = iff(QueryCount > 0, round(100.0 * toreal(LongNameCount) / toreal(QueryCount), 1), 0.0)
| order by QueryCount desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: FortiGate DNS query telemetry: volume per internal host, the share of responses that did not resolve, and the length of the queried name. Long names with a high NXDOMAIN rate are the classic DNS tunnelling shape, where data is encoded into subdomains to smuggle it out. FortiGate only carries the queried name and the response code, so the entropy signal here is length and repetition, not character distribution.

properties.displayName: CSL Hunt FQ09 - FortiGate Policy Hit Analysis
properties.query:
let lookback = 7d;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| extend PolicyId = extract(@"policyid=([^ ]+)", 1, tostring(AdditionalExtensions))
| extend Action   = tolower(tostring(DeviceAction))
| summarize
    TotalEvents   = count(),
    AcceptedCount = countif(Action in ("accept", "allowed", "allow")),
    DeniedCount   = countif(Action in ("deny", "drop", "blocked", "reject")),
    SourceIPs     = dcount(SourceIP),
    DestIPs       = dcount(DestinationIP),
    Apps          = make_set(ApplicationProtocol, 5),
    FirstSeen     = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen      = max(TimeGenerated)
  by PolicyId
| order by TotalEvents desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Which FortiGate policies are carrying traffic, how much, and which are carrying none. An unused policy is attack surface that is maintained but never exercised, and a policy carrying an unexpected volume of denied traffic is often the policy an attacker is testing. The policy id is read from the policyid key in AdditionalExtensions.

properties.displayName: CSL Hunt FQ10 - FortiGate Traffic Anomaly and Denial of Service Events

let anomalySubtypes = dynamic(["forward-anomaly", "ips-anomaly", "av-anomaly",
                                "botnet", "dos", "flood", "anomaly", "tcp-psh",
                                "udp-flood", "icmp-flood"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where tolower(Activity) in (anomalySubtypes)
    or tolower(DeviceEventClassID) in ("traffic-anomaly", "anomaly")
| extend SrcCountry = tostring(geo_info_from_ip_address(SourceIP).country_2)
| summarize
    EventCount    = count(),
    SourceIPs     = make_set(SourceIP, 20),
    DestIPs       = make_set(DestinationIP, 20),
    SrcCountries  = make_set(SrcCountry, 5),
    Actions       = make_set(DeviceAction, 5),
    Severities    = make_set(LogSeverity, 5),
    FirstSeen     = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen      = max(TimeGenerated)
  by Activity, SrcCountry
| order by EventCount desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: FortiGate traffic anomaly, IPS anomaly and botnet events, which are the gateway's own view of a flood, a scan storm or a compromised host talking to known bad infrastructure. These subtypes are FortiGate specific and are not visible as IPS signature hits, so a rule that only looks at signatures misses them entirely.

properties.displayName: CSL Hunt FQ11 - FortiGate DLP Sensitive Data Matches
properties.query:
let lookback = 7d;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where tolower(Activity) == "dlp" or tolower(DeviceEventClassID) == "dlp"
| extend DLPPattern = extract(@"catdesc=([^ ]+)", 1, tostring(AdditionalExtensions))
| extend DLPPattern = iff(isempty(DLPPattern), "unclassified", DLPPattern)
| extend Action     = tolower(tostring(DeviceAction))
| summarize
    HitCount       = count(),
    BlockedCount   = countif(Action == "blocked"),
    AllowedCount   = countif(Action == "accept"),
    Users          = make_set(SourceUserName, 20),
    SourceIPs      = make_set(SourceIP, 20),
    DestHostNames  = make_set(DestinationHostName, 10),
    Apps           = make_set(ApplicationProtocol, 5),
    FirstSeen      = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen       = max(TimeGenerated)
  by DLPPattern
| extend BlockRate = iff(HitCount > 0, round(100.0 * toreal(BlockedCount) / toreal(HitCount), 1), 0.0)
| order by HitCount desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: FortiGate DLP events where a sensitive data pattern matched traffic. The DLP subsystem inspects content on the wire, so a match means the data actually crossed the boundary, whether the policy allowed it. The matched pattern is read from catdesc in AdditionalExtensions.

properties.displayName: CSL Hunt FQ12 - FortiGate Application Control - Risk Categories
properties.query:
let lookback = 7d;
let riskApps = dynamic(["bittorrent", "torrent", "p2p", "anonymizer", "anonymiser",
                         "proxy", "socks", "tor", "personal.cloud", "dropbox",
                         "onedrive", "mega", "telegram", "whatsapp", "discord",
                         "steam", "skype", "facebook", "youtube", "spotify"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where tolower(DeviceEventClassID) == "app-ctrl" or tolower(Activity) == "appctrl"
| extend DetectedApp = tolower(tostring(ApplicationProtocol))
| extend Action      = tolower(tostring(DeviceAction))
| summarize
    HitCount       = count(),
    BlockedCount   = countif(Action == "blocked"),
    AllowedCount   = countif(Action == "accept"),
    Users          = make_set(SourceUserName, 20),
    SourceIPs      = make_set(SourceIP, 20),
    DestHostNames  = make_set(DestinationHostName, 10),
    FirstSeen      = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen       = max(TimeGenerated)
  by DetectedApp
| where DetectedApp in (riskApps)
| extend BlockRate = iff(HitCount > 0, round(100.0 * toreal(BlockedCount) / toreal(HitCount), 1), 0.0)
| order by HitCount desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: FortiGate application control events grouped by the application that was identified, showing which risky categories the estate is actually using. Peer to peer, torrent, anonymiser and personal cloud storage categories are the ones that break both exfiltration and security controls at the same time.

properties.displayName: CSL Hunt FQ13 - FortiGate Internal to Internal Traffic (Zone Pivoting)
properties.query:
let lookback = 24h;
let adminPorts = dynamic(["22", "23", "135", "139", "445", "3389", "5985", "5986",
                           "1433", "3306", "5432", "1521"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where isnotempty(SourceIP) and isnotempty(DestinationIP)
| where ipv4_is_private(SourceIP) == true
| where ipv4_is_private(DestinationIP) == true
| where SourceIP != DestinationIP
| extend DstPort = tostring(DestinationPort)
| summarize
    SessionCount     = count(),
    UniqueTargets    = dcount(DestinationIP),
    UniquePorts      = dcount(DstPort),
    AdminPortHits    = countif(DstPort in (adminPorts)),
    AcceptedSessions = countif(tolower(DeviceAction) in ("accept", "allowed", "allow")),
    TargetIPs        = make_set(DestinationIP, 30),
    PortsUsed        = make_set(DstPort, 10),
    Users            = make_set(SourceUserName, 10),
    FirstSeen        = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen         = max(TimeGenerated)
  by SourceIP
| where UniqueTargets > 5
| order by UniqueTargets desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Internal-to-internal sessions observed by the FortiGate, broken down by port and source. This is the only place most estates see east-west traffic at all, because endpoint telemetry does not cross the firewall boundary. A host talking to many internal targets on admin ports is the lateral movement signal that the perimeter denies cannot see.

properties.displayName: CSL Hunt FQ14 - FortiGate FortiClient Endpoint Telemetry
properties.query:
let lookback = 7d;
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where tolower(Activity) has_any ("fct-")
    or tolower(DeviceEventClassID) has_any ("fct-")
    or tolower(DeviceEventID) has_any ("0100", "0110")
| summarize
    EventCount     = count(),
    Endpoints      = dcount(SourceIP),
    Users          = make_set(SourceUserName, 10),
    Apps           = make_set(ApplicationProtocol, 5),
    Actions        = make_set(DeviceAction, 5),
    Severities     = make_set(LogSeverity, 5),
    FirstSeen      = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen       = max(TimeGenerated)
  by Activity
| order by EventCount desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: FortiClient managed endpoint telemetry - the fct-traffic, fct-utm and fct-event log types. This is the FortiGate side of endpoint visibility and it is usually the only source that survives an attacker disabling a security tool. An estate with FortiClient deployed but no fct-* logs arriving has a blind spot, and this query makes that visible.

properties.displayName: CSL Hunt FQ15 - FortiGate External Inbound Session Exposure
properties.query:
let lookback = 24h;
let exposedServicePorts = dynamic(["22", "23", "135", "139", "445", "1433", "3306",
                                    "5432", "3389", "5985", "5986", "8080", "8443",
                                    "9200", "27017", "6379", "11211"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DeviceVendor == "Fortinet"
| where tolower(DeviceAction) in ("accept", "allowed", "allow")
| where isnotempty(SourceIP) and isnotempty(DestinationIP)
| where ipv4_is_private(SourceIP) == false
| where ipv4_is_private(DestinationIP) == true
| extend DstPort = tostring(DestinationPort)
| extend SrcCountry = tostring(geo_info_from_ip_address(SourceIP).country_2)
| summarize
    SessionCount    = count(),
    ExternalSources = dcount(SourceIP),
    SrcCountries    = make_set(SrcCountry, 5),
    SourceIPs       = make_set(SourceIP, 20),
    Users           = make_set(SourceUserName, 10),
    Apps            = make_set(ApplicationProtocol, 5),
    FirstSeen       = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen        = max(TimeGenerated)
  by DestinationIP, DstPort
| where DstPort in (exposedServicePorts)
| order by SessionCount desc

tags.name: description
tags.value: Internet-facing sessions the FortiGate permitted, grouped by the internal host that was reached and the port it was reached on. Anything here is a service that is exposed to the internet. Management interfaces, databases and file shares showing up in this list are findings in their own right, independent of whether anyone has attacked them yet.
